title: Recording with visiting stars; Minnie the Moocher
summary: He sings Hi-de-ho on a Cab Calloway session and estimates 2,000 tunes a year.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Now, you were saying after you shaved your beard off after being fired a couple times, you were telling me something about people would come in on the shows and what happened? Guys like --

Oh, yeah. Well, this was as early as when I first left CBS. You know, when I got fired, actually it was a lucky break because I got into the commercial field, the outside field as they called it, which I might not have had the nerve to make the move on my own. And I had a lot of satisfactions, I got to record with people I admired. Because what would happen would be lots of times they would

want to record a band and the leader would be out of Chicago or someplace, and he would fly into New York and pick up a studio band. Now, if it was a star like, say, Cab Calloway or somebody where he was the star more than the band was, though God knows he had a marvelous -- well, you were in the band for a long time. That was one of the great bands of all times, had the Palmer Brothers and everything. Gee, that was a good band, Tyree and Dizzy and all those people, Jonah Jones, God, what a band.
But he would come in and it was a kick for me, it was a wonderful experience because I made a record of "Minnie the Moocher" with him, I got to sing, "Hidi, Hidi, Ho."
I figured once that I had made about -- well, you figure on a date you made four sides on each date, and did ten a week, I made 40 tunes a week, which would be 2,000 tunes a year for 25 years.

So some kid asked me, do you have all the records you made, and I said, no, I don't have any of them. Well, that's not quite true, one of the few I have is Cab Calloway's record with me singing Hidi Ho.
